intro.title: The BINH BFC story
intro.body: Founded in 2010 in Dong Nai, BINH BFC makes outdoor furniture for resorts, hotels and distributors. Our 28,000 m² factory and 370 people handle every step in house, from aluminum, steel and teak frames to rope and wicker weaving and cushion sewing. That keeps quality and lead times under our control at every stage, on every order.

about.title: Beautiful and durable outdoor furniture
about.p1: BINH BFC are created with a goal to make beautiful and durable outdoor furniture. Our strength is to mix and match different medium such as teak, aluminum, steel, resin wicker and rope to achieve the desirable aesthetic that customers require.
about.p2: We have a total of 370 employees with rich experiences in metalworking, woodworking, and weaving. Our total factory area is around 28,000 m².

MaterialsPage.metaDescription: FSC teak, aluminium, steel, rope, resin wicker, fabric, glass and ceramic: the materials BFC uses for outdoor furniture.

hero.title: Materials
hero.lede: Teak, aluminium, steel, rope, resin wicker, fabric, glass and ceramic: the materials behind BFC outdoor furniture. Choose a material to see the details.

wood.lede: Plantation teak with FSC certification, sourced from Costa Rica and Brazil. Its natural oils let teak stand up to sun, rain and humidity outdoors, which is why it is BFC's core material.
properties: Teak is rich in natural oils and resins, so it absorbs little water, resists warping and keeps insects away without heavy chemical treatment.
Left outdoors, the surface gradually turns from honey brown to silver grey. This natural patina does not affect the strength of the wood. Indoors or under cover, teak keeps its brown tone for longer.
craft: Blanks are selected and grain matched, dried to 8-12% moisture and shaped on 5-axis CNC. Joints are cut and fitted precisely before sanding from coarse to fine.
All woodworking happens inside the factory, alongside weaving, upholstery and packing, so a teak frame never leaves the site before it becomes a finished piece.
care: Teak is an oily wood, so it should not be painted or varnished. Any coating will flake over time as the natural oils rise to the surface.
Clean regularly with warm water, mild soap and a soft brush, working along the grain, then let it dry naturally. Do not use a pressure washer.
To keep the honey tone of new teak, use a dedicated teak oil or protector following the maker's instructions.
When storing through the rainy season or winter, keep furniture somewhere dry and ventilated. Avoid airtight covers, which trap moisture.

aluminum.lede: Extruded aluminium, fabricated and powder coated in our own factory. Light, rustproof and able to hold the slim lines that wood cannot.
properties: Aluminium is light, so pieces are easy to move, stack and ship. It does not rust like iron based metals, which suits hot, humid climates and coastal sites.
Powder coating gives an even colour that resists scratches and is easy to clean. Aluminium frames are also the base for our rope and wicker.
craft: Tubes are laser cut to drawing, bent to radius, robot welded at main joints and hand welded at hidden ones, then the welds are ground flush.
Before coating, every frame passes a 6-stage pretreatment line: alkaline degreasing, two water rinses, a nano-zincofin layer, a final rinse and drying. The frame is then powder coated and oven cured.
care: Wipe with a soft cloth, water and a neutral soap, rinse with clean water and dry.
Avoid strong detergents, solvents and abrasive pads, which can dull or scratch the coating.
Near the sea, rinse off salt deposits more often to keep the coating durable.
If the coating is deeply scratched, touch it up early with matching paint to protect the surrounding surface.

rope.lede: Outdoor grade polypropylene rope, hand woven by our weavers onto teak or powder coated aluminium frames.
properties: The rope resists UV, mould and weather, staying soft and holding its colour outdoors.
A woven rope surface has a gentle give, feels soft and breathes, and makes a piece look lighter than a solid frame.
craft: The frame is fixed on a jig, and weavers pull each strand to a standard pattern, adjusting the tension by hand. Ends are locked and hidden for a clean finish.
Rope weaving is entirely manual, a skill no machine can replace. Tension is checked before the piece moves on to upholstery or packing.
care: Brush off dust and leaves regularly. When needed, clean with warm water, mild soap and a soft brush, then rinse with clean water.
Let the rope dry fully before adding cushions or a cover, to prevent mould.
Avoid strong detergents and pressure washers, which can fray the fibres.
Store somewhere dry and ventilated when not in use for long periods.

wicker.lede: Extruded polyethylene fibre, kiln dried to hold its colour, woven onto pretreated, powder coated aluminium frames.
properties: Resin wicker keeps the warmth of natural rattan without rotting, cracking or absorbing water outdoors.
Woven pieces carry a standard 2-year warranty, extendable beyond 5 years on request.
craft: Frames are powder coated first, so the surface is hard enough to take tension without scratching. Weavers pull the fibre to pattern, adjust tension and lock the ends by hand.
From dense, closed weaves to open patterns that show the frame, weaves can be developed to each customer's drawings.
care: Dust regularly. When needed, clean with warm water, mild soap and a soft brush, then rinse with clean water.
Let the weave dry fully before adding cushions or a cover.
Avoid strong detergents, solvents and sharp objects on the weave.
Store somewhere dry and ventilated when not in use for long periods.

steel.lede: Steel is used where parts need high stiffness and load capacity, such as bases, table frames and connecting members.
properties: Steel's stiffness allows slim bases and frames that stay stable, well suited to tables with stone, ceramic or glass tops.
Outdoors, steel needs the right surface protection. The finish determines how well a piece stands up to moisture and weather.
craft: Steel parts are cut, welded and ground to drawing, then surface treated and finished before assembly.
Material specifications and finishing processes are agreed with each customer at the quotation and sampling stage.
care: Wipe with a soft cloth, water and a neutral soap, then dry completely.
Check spots where water can collect, such as bases and joints. If the finish is scratched, treat it early to stop rust spreading.
Near the sea, rinse off salt deposits more often.
Avoid acidic cleaners and abrasive pads.

fabric.lede: Outdoor fabric for seat cushions, back cushions and pillows, cut and sewn in the factory's upholstery workshop.
properties: Outdoor fabrics are made to withstand sun, dry quickly and resist mould, holding colour better than standard indoor fabrics.
Colours and fabric types can follow a collection or a customer's own specification.
craft: Fabric and foam are cut to pattern, sewn into covers, filled and shaped before the final seams are closed.
The upholstery workshop sits next to the woodworking and weaving shops, so cushions are fitted to their frames inside the factory.
care: Brush off dust and treat stains early with warm water and mild soap, blotting rather than scrubbing.
Stand cushions on their edge after rain so water drains quickly, and let them dry fully before storing.
When not in use, store cushions somewhere dry or in a breathable storage bag.
Check each fabric's care label before washing covers.

glass.lede: Glass for dining, coffee and side table tops, paired with aluminium, steel or teak frames.
properties: A glass top is flat, non absorbent and easy to clean, making an outdoor space feel open and light.
Glass lets the eye travel down to the base, so it is often chosen to show off the frame beneath.
craft: Glass tops are ordered to drawing, and edges and surfaces are checked on arrival before fitting to the frame.
Pads and fixings between glass and frame are specified so the top sits firmly without touching metal directly.
care: Wipe with a soft cloth and clean water or glass cleaner, avoiding abrasive pads.
Do not place hot items directly on the glass, and avoid hard knocks to the edges.
Check the pads between glass and frame regularly and replace them if they age.
When storing, lay the top on a flat surface with nothing heavy stacked on it.

ceramic.lede: Ceramic tops for outdoor dining and coffee tables, with the look of natural stone and easier care.
properties: Ceramic has a hard surface that resists heat and scratches, stains little and does not absorb water.
A wide range of patterns and colours, from stone veining to plain surfaces, pairs easily with aluminium, steel or teak frames.
craft: Ceramic tops are checked on arrival, then fitted to the table frame with suitable pads and fixings.
Size, thickness and edge profile are agreed to each project's drawings.
care: Wipe with a damp cloth and neutral soap, then dry.
Wipe up oil, wine or coffee promptly so they leave no marks.
Avoid hard knocks to edges and corners.
Avoid strong acidic cleaners and abrasive pads.

AboutPage.metaDescription: BINH BFC has made outdoor furniture in Dong Nai, Vietnam since 2010: a 28,000 m² factory and 370 people working wood, aluminum, steel, rope, resin wicker and upholstery in house.

hero.title: About BINH BFC
hero.lede: An outdoor furniture manufacturer in Dong Nai, Vietnam since 2010. We build to your drawings and co-develop designs for hotels, resorts and furniture brands.

story.title: Our story
story.lead: Lasting outdoor furniture is made of every weld, every grain of wood and every strand of weave. BINH BFC was founded to do all of that under one roof.
paragraphs: Founded in 2010 in Dong Nai, BINH BFC started with a clear aim: outdoor furniture that looks good and stands up to sun, rain and humidity all year round. Since then our clients have been resorts, hotels, distributors and furniture brands that need a factory to build exactly to drawing and on schedule.

Our strength is combining materials in a single piece: teak, aluminum, steel, resin wicker, rope and outdoor fabric. Each material has its own workshop on the same site, so a chair can move from aluminum frame to powder coating, to the weaving floor and on to upholstery without leaving the factory.

Working in house means we see the product at every step. When something needs fixing, the people before and after that step stand in the same place to solve it, instead of waiting on feedback across several suppliers.

Today our 28,000 m² factory and 370 people keep that way of working: carpenters, welders, weavers and upholsterers work directly on each client's product, from the first prototype to the last container.

values.title: What we hold to
values.lede: Four principles that shape how BINH BFC handles every order.

inhouse.name: Made in house
inhouse.desc: Wood, metal, weaving, coating, upholstery and packing all sit on one site. We control quality and schedule instead of relying on outside subcontractors.

materials.name: Knowing each material
materials.desc: Every material has its own workshop and team. Knowing how wood moves and how aluminum must be treated is what lets us combine them so they last.

partner.name: Built to your drawings
partner.desc: We manufacture for our clients' brands. Drawings, samples and specifications are kept exactly as approved, with engineering feedback when it helps.

outdoor.name: Made for outdoors
outdoor.desc: Every choice of material, joint and finish serves one goal: furniture that holds up for years in sun, rain and salt air.

people.title: The people in our workshops
body: Behind every piece is a team of 370, most of them working on the factory floor. Many steps, such as rope weaving, wicker weaving and wood finishing, still need the hands and eye of a skilled maker.
We invest in machines where precision must repeat, such as 5-axis CNC for wood and laser cutting and robotic welding for metal, so our makers can spend their time on the details machines cannot do.

export.title: From Dong Nai to your project
body: The factory has its own container yard on site. Goods are inspected, packed and loaded right here, so we control the last step before anything leaves the factory.
Every order has one contact who follows it from the first drawing to shipping day, so you always know which stage your products are at.
